title: Can a Higher Dimensional Model of the Universe Solve the Problem of Dark Matter?
content: We show that the effects usually attributed to the presence of dark matter in the Universe can arise from the ``external'' effect on our Universe due to extra dimensions. For this, we consider a braneworld scenario where our universe, which is a 3-brane, is immersed in a 6D Minkowski bulk. We derive the $1/r$ force on the 3-brane at large distances via the on-brane propagator. This scaling reproduces the effect of dark matter, such as the flat rotation curves of galaxies and a higher deflection angle around some gravitational lenses. It also explains the large-scale structure formation of the universe. This approach thus offers a novel perspective on dark matter, suggesting that higher-dimensional physics can account for these cosmic phenomena.
